nodes.summary: For every set $A$ of natural numbers with positive upper density, that is, with $\limsup_{N \to \infty} |A \cap \{0, \dots, N - 1\}| / N > 0$, there are an infinite set $B \subseteq A$ and an integer $t$ such that $b_1 + b_2 + t \in A$ for all distinct $b_1, b_2 \in B$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 656 is true

nodes.summary: The statement that for every set $A$ of natural numbers with positive upper density, that is, with $\limsup_{N \to \infty} |A \cap \{0, \dots, N - 1\}| / N > 0$, there are an infinite set $B \subseteq A$ and an integer $t$ such that $b_1 + b_2 + t \in A$ for all distinct $b_1, b_2 \in B$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 656 (shifted restricted sumsets in dense sets)
